subject: Numeracy
title: Round things
subtopics: Drawing a circle in the air and in sand
objectives: Children will find round things in the classroom and outdoors.
Children will name the circle with support.
content: Finding, handling and naming circles and round things such as balls, plates and wheels.
teachingActivities: Hold round objects up and say "round, circle"; trace the edge slowly with a finger; let children roll and feel the objects before naming.
learnerActivities: Find round things, roll and not-roll objects, trace circles with fingers and draw circles in sand or the air.
resources: Balls, plates, plastic bowls, a toy wheel
Blocks and boxes that do not roll
A tray of sand or flour
Chalk or a stick for outdoor drawing
assessment: Note who points to round objects when asked and who says circle or round.
expectedOutcomes: Points to round objects when asked.
crossCurricular: Literacy: shape names in a rhyme
Physical Development: tracing and arm movements

lessons.title: Round like a ball
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will point to round things and say round or circle with support.
successCriteria: Points to a round object when asked
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three with real things and sort by colour, size and kind.
resources: A ball, a plate, a bowl, a toy wheel
lessons.starter: Roll a ball slowly across the floor. Say "Round, round, round!" Show the other objects and let the children pick out which look like the ball.
teacherActivities: Hold up the ball, plate and wheel and trace their edges with your finger. Say "Round. A circle."
Hold up the block and the box. Say "Not round. Not a circle."
Put all objects in the basket. Ask a child to pick one round object.
Place all round objects on one mat and the others on another mat.
learnerActivities: Children trace the air with their fingers and say "round".
Children shake their heads or say "no".
Child chooses a round object and shows the group.
Children help to sort round from not round.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up the ball, plate and wheel and trace their edges with your finger. Say "Round. A circle." Children: Children trace the air with their fingers and say "round".
Step 2. Teacher: Hold up the block and the box. Say "Not round. Not a circle." Children: Children shake their heads or say "no".
Step 3. Teacher: Put all objects in the basket. Ask a child to pick one round object. Children: Child chooses a round object and shows the group.
Step 4. Teacher: Place all round objects on one mat and the others on another mat. Children: Children help to sort round from not round.

practical.title: Round thing hunt
steps: Set several objects around the room, round and not round.
Children find one round thing and bring it to the mat.
The group checks by tracing the edge.
practical.safety: Remove sharp or breakable objects; use plates and bowls made of plastic. Children carry one object at a time.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects only, a ball and a box, and guide the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three round things and name each one.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Which one is round?
questions.expected: Child points to the ball, plate or wheel.

lessons.conclusion: Sing the circle song and trace a big circle in the air with both arms.
lessons.homeConnection: Find round things at home, such as plates, cups, clocks and coins held by an adult, and say "round".
teacherReflection: Which children could show "point to round things and say round or circle with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

pictures: A ball, a plate and a wheel
A box and a block (not round)
learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Round, round, round, like a ball. Round, round, round, like a plate. Circle, circle, round and round.

lessons.title: Roll or not roll?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will test which objects roll and which do not.
successCriteria: Says roll or stop with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three with real things and sort by colour, size and kind.
resources: A ball, a tin or round container, a block, a box
A gentle slope such as a tilted board
lessons.starter: Push a ball and a block together and ask "Which one rolled? Which one stayed?" Let the children watch.
teacherActivities: Push the ball. Say "It rolls!" Push the block and say "It does not roll."
Let children push each object in turn along the floor.
Set up a gentle slope and let the objects slide or roll down.
Sort the objects into "rolls" and "does not roll" baskets.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say "roll" or "no roll".
Child pushes the object and watches it move or stay.
Children say "roll" when the object rolls.
Child places each object in the correct basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Push the ball. Say "It rolls!" Push the block and say "It does not roll." Children: Children watch and say "roll" or "no roll".
Step 2. Teacher: Let children push each object in turn along the floor. Children: Child pushes the object and watches it move or stay.
Step 3. Teacher: Set up a gentle slope and let the objects slide or roll down. Children: Children say "roll" when the object rolls.
Step 4. Teacher: Sort the objects into "rolls" and "does not roll" baskets. Children: Child places each object in the correct basket.

practical.title: Roll test
steps: Give each pair a ball and a block.
They push both and see which rolls.
They put the round one in the basket.
practical.safety: Use a gentle slope only; keep fingers away from the end of the board. Clear the floor so children do not trip over rolling objects.

differentiation.support: Offer only the ball and block with an adult pushing alongside.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to predict whether a new object will roll before pushing it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Roll the ball one more time and say "Round things roll."
lessons.homeConnection: At home, test which objects roll along the floor: a ball, a tin and a box.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "test which objects roll and which do not" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Drawing circles in sand
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Drawing a circle in the air and in sand
objectives: Children will trace and draw a circle in sand or on a tray.
successCriteria: Traces a round shape with a finger
Draws a circle-like shape in sand
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three with real things and sort by colour, size and kind.
resources: A tray of dry sand or flour
Chalk or a stick for outdoor drawing
lessons.starter: Draw a big circle in the air with your finger. Say "Round and round." Invite the children to draw circles in the air with you.
teacherActivities: Draw a circle in the sand with your finger, slowly, and say "round and round".
Give each child a tray. Say "Draw a round shape."
Show a paper circle and match it to the one in the sand.
Wipe the trays and try again with a bigger circle.
learnerActivities: Children watch and trace the circle with their own fingers.
Child draws in the sand with a finger.
Child compares and points to the match.
Child draws a larger circle and shows a friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Draw a circle in the sand with your finger, slowly, and say "round and round". Children: Children watch and trace the circle with their own fingers.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a tray. Say "Draw a round shape." Children: Child draws in the sand with a finger.
Step 3. Teacher: Show a paper circle and match it to the one in the sand. Children: Child compares and points to the match.
Step 4. Teacher: Wipe the trays and try again with a bigger circle. Children: Child draws a larger circle and shows a friend.

practical.title: Sand circle trays
steps: Give each child a shallow tray of sand.
Draw round shapes with a finger.
Gently shake the tray to wipe it clean.
practical.safety: Use clean, dry sand or flour; tell children not to eat it or throw it. Wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Use hand-over-hand tracing around a paper circle.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to draw two circles and say which is bigger.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Draws or traces a circle shape
lessons.conclusion: Wipe the sand smooth and say "All gone circle. Goodbye."
lessons.homeConnection: Trace around a plate or a cup with your child to make a circle.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "trace and draw a circle in sand or on a tray" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Circles in the market
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find circles in a pretend market and in the outdoor environment.
successCriteria: Points to circles in a play market
Says circle or round in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three with real things and sort by colour, size and kind.
resources: Toy oranges, tomatoes, a round tray, a plate, a bowl
lessons.starter: Set up the market and say "Today the market sells round things only. Can you help me find them?"
teacherActivities: Show an orange and a tomato. Say "Round like a ball. A circle."
Ask a child to be the customer and buy something round from the stall.
Swap roles and let others buy round things and name them.
Take the group outdoors and point out round things such as a wheel or a tin.
learnerActivities: Children touch the fruits and say "round".
Child picks a round object and gives it to the trader.
Children buy and say "round" or "circle".
Children find and name round things outside.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show an orange and a tomato. Say "Round like a ball. A circle." Children: Children touch the fruits and say "round".
Step 2. Teacher: Ask a child to be the customer and buy something round from the stall. Children: Child picks a round object and gives it to the trader.
Step 3. Teacher: Swap roles and let others buy round things and name them. Children: Children buy and say "round" or "circle".
Step 4. Teacher: Take the group outdoors and point out round things such as a wheel or a tin. Children: Children find and name round things outside.

practical.title: Round market
steps: Place a mix of round and not round objects on the stall.
They tell the trader what they bought.
practical.safety: Use toy or washed fruits that cannot be swallowed. Hold the outdoor walk within a fenced, supervised area.

differentiation.support: Offer only two items and guide the child to choose the round one.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sell something round to a friend and name it.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What round thing did you buy?
Is this a circle?
questions.expected: Yes or no depending on the object.

lessons.conclusion: Put all round things in the basket and say "Circle, circle, round."
lessons.homeConnection: Spot round things when you go to the market, such as oranges and wheels.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find circles in a pretend market and in the outdoor environment" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Round things stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will find, roll and trace circles at three stations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to three with real things and sort by colour, size and kind.
lessons.starter: Sing the circle song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station.
Ask each observed child "Which is round?" and "Does it roll?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child points and answers.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask each observed child "Which is round?" and "Does it roll?" Children: Child points and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove small items; supervise every station.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a friend in the roll test.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: points to round objects; says circle or round; tests roll and not roll.

questions.question: Show me something round.
questions.expected: Child points to a round object.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Sing the circle song and draw a big circle in the air together.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for round things on the way home and name them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find, roll and trace circles at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
